Thanks for the earlier call. As Veridian moves toward a pilot with Redwood Private, our compliance team needs a concise attestation that explains how network boundaries are enforced between customer tenancy and shared control plane for both Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically we're looking for: 

- A short narrative (1–2 pages) describing isolation controls and threat model assumptions.
- A diagram legend that maps network layers (control plane, management, tenant data plane, egress) to controls.
- A minimal evidence set (config snippets or references) that demonstrates VLANs/VPCs, routing controls, and KMS boundary handling.

Can you provide this by end of day Monday or point us to the right package? If you have any limitations (redacted diagrams, NDA constraints), let us know so we can plan our SOC2 intake.

Thanks — Anya

Subject: DRAFT — network boundary attestation (for review)

Olga / Soojin — attaching a draft narrative below and a short legend I plan to convert to the PDF. TL;DR: Redwood enforces tenant isolation between control plane and tenant data plane via separate VPCs/subnets, dedicated routing tables, and a strict egress gateway controlled by KMS-scoped keys. For Dedicated we additionally pin tenant workloads to reserved GPU pools with isolated overlay routing.

Questions for Veridian we should confirm before finalizing: 
- Are they intending to use Private (customer-managed VPC with our appliance) or Redwood-Hosted Dedicated? The evidence set differs slightly.
- Do they require public egress IP allowlisting or NAT-based shared egress?

Draft narrative (excerpt):
"Redwood's boundary model for Private and Dedicated deployments separates logical planes: (1) Control plane — customer management APIs and telemetry; (2) Tenant data plane — model inference pods and KV caches; (3) Management/ops plane — image registry and orchestration; (4) Egress gateway — monitored and policy-enforced path to external services. Each plane operates in distinct network segments with enforced routing and ACLs; cross-plane access is mediated by tightly scoped service accounts and KMS-wrapped credentials. For Dedicated deployments, tenant compute runs in reserved pools with overlay-fabric routing to guarantee isolation at the network fabric level.

Legend highlights:
- Control plane: isolated VPC, private endpoints, limited peering to ops VPC.
- Tenant data plane: per-tenant VPC/subnet tagging, ephemeral compute, KV cache with in-memory encryption.
- Egress gateway: TLS termination + egress proxy, TLS mutual auth when required.

I will attach the segmentation attribute matrix next (redacted). Marcus — FYI I included the overlay note you requested.

-- Karthik
Network & Infrastructure Lead | Redwood Inference
